s_pyramids.name: Pyramids of Giza
s_pyramids.description: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world. Go at opening time to beat the heat and the crowds, then ride out into the desert for the classic three-pyramid panorama.

s_egyptian_museum.name: The Egyptian Museum
s_egyptian_museum.description: Home to Tutankhamun's treasures and floor after floor of antiquities. A must for history lovers — allow at least half a day.

s_khan.name: Khan el-Khalili
s_khan.description: A labyrinthine medieval bazaar of lanterns, spices and silver. Haggle hard, then collapse into a mint tea at a backstreet café.

s_azhar_park.name: Al-Azhar Park
s_azhar_park.description: A green oasis with sweeping views over Islamic Cairo's minarets and the Citadel. Perfect for golden hour.

s_abou_tarek.name: Koshary Abou Tarek
s_abou_tarek.description: The most famous koshary in the city — a comforting bowl of rice, lentils, pasta and crispy onions. Cheap, vegetarian, unforgettable.

s_fishawy.name: El Fishawy Café
s_fishawy.description: A 200-year-old café tucked in the bazaar, all mirrors and mint tea and shisha smoke. A literary haunt that feels frozen in time.

s_cairo_tower.name: Cairo Tower
s_cairo_tower.description: 187 metres above the city with a 360° view of the Nile threading through Cairo. Best as the sun drops and the lights come on.

s_brandenburg.name: Brandenburg Gate
s_brandenburg.description: Berlin's neoclassical icon and a symbol of reunification. Stunning when floodlit at night and blissfully crowd-free at dawn.

s_museum_island.name: Museum Island
s_museum_island.description: A UNESCO ensemble of five world-class museums on a Spree island, from the Pergamon's ancient altars to the bust of Nefertiti.

s_markthalle.name: Markthalle Neun
s_markthalle.description: A restored 1891 market hall. Come on Street Food Thursday and graze your way around the world, one stall at a time.

s_tempelhof.name: Tempelhofer Feld
s_tempelhof.description: A decommissioned airport turned vast public park. Cycle the runways, fly a kite, or join the urban gardeners at sunset.

s_klunkerkranich.name: Klunkerkranich
s_klunkerkranich.description: A rooftop bar and garden hidden atop a shopping-centre car park in Neukölln. Sundowners, DJs and one of the best skyline views in the city.

s_eiffel.name: Eiffel Tower
s_eiffel.description: The grande dame of Paris. Watch from the Champ de Mars as she sparkles for five minutes on the hour after dark.

s_louvre.name: Musée du Louvre
s_louvre.description: The world's most-visited museum. Pick two or three wings, book ahead, and don't miss the courtyard pyramid at night.

s_marais_cafe.name: Café in Le Marais
s_marais_cafe.description: Cobbled lanes, vintage boutiques and the best falafel in the city. Grab a corner table and watch the most stylish street in Paris drift by.

s_montmartre.name: Montmartre & Sacré-Cœur
s_montmartre.description: Climb the hill of artists to the white domes of Sacré-Cœur and the finest free view over Paris. Lose yourself in the lanes behind it.

s_colosseum.name: Colosseum
s_colosseum.description: The mighty amphitheatre of ancient Rome. Book a skip-the-line slot and add the underground tour to stand where gladiators waited.

s_trastevere.name: Trastevere
s_trastevere.description: Rome's most charming quarter — ivy-clad lanes, trattorias and piazzas that come alive after dark. The place for an unhurried Roman dinner.

s_pantheon.name: Pantheon
s_pantheon.description: A 2,000-year-old temple with the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome and an oculus open to the sky. Free, breathtaking, central.

s_citadel.name: Salah El-Din Citadel
s_citadel.description: A medieval Islamic fortress crowned by the alabaster Mohamed Ali Mosque, with the whole city sprawling below.

s_felucca.name: Nile Felucca Sunset Sail
s_felucca.description: Hire a traditional wooden sailboat at golden hour and drift past Zamalek as the city lights flicker on.

s_east_side.name: East Side Gallery
s_east_side.description: The longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall, now a 1.3km open-air gallery of murals — including the famous fraternal kiss.

s_reichstag.name: Reichstag Dome
s_reichstag.description: Norman Foster's glass dome over the German parliament — free to visit with a booking, spiralling up to a 360° city panorama.

s_orsay.name: Musée d'Orsay
s_orsay.description: Impressionist heaven in a beaux-arts railway station — Monet, Van Gogh and Degas under a giant glass clock.

s_seine.name: Seine Riverbanks
s_seine.description: Stroll the UNESCO-listed quays past bouquinistes and bridges; picnic by the water as the Eiffel Tower sparkles.

s_trevi.name: Trevi Fountain
s_trevi.description: Rome's most theatrical baroque fountain. Toss a coin over your shoulder and you're destined to return.

s_vatican.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
s_vatican.description: Mile after mile of treasures ending in Michelangelo's ceiling. Book the first slot or a Friday-night opening.

s_tower_bridge.name: Tower Bridge
s_tower_bridge.description: London's Victorian icon over the Thames. Walk the high-level glass floor and time it for a bridge lift.

s_british_museum.name: The British Museum
s_british_museum.description: From the Rosetta Stone to the Parthenon marbles — two million years of history, and entry is free.

s_borough.name: Borough Market
s_borough.description: A 1,000-year-old food market under railway arches — artisan cheese, salt-beef bagels and sizzling street food.

s_sky_garden.name: Sky Garden
s_sky_garden.description: A free three-storey rooftop garden with floor-to-ceiling views across the City — book a slot in advance.

s_camden.name: Camden Market
s_camden.description: Punk-spirited maze of stalls, vintage and global street eats along the canal in Camden Town.

s_sagrada.name: Sagrada Família
s_sagrada.description: Gaudí's still-unfinished basilica — a forest of stone columns lit by kaleidoscope stained glass. Book a timed ticket.

s_park_guell.name: Park Güell
s_park_guell.description: Gaudí's mosaic dreamscape on a hill — the serpentine bench and terrace frame the whole city and sea.

s_boqueria.name: Mercat de la Boqueria
s_boqueria.description: A riot of colour off La Rambla — jamón, fresh juices and tapas bars where locals grab breakfast at the counter.

s_barceloneta.name: Barceloneta Beach
s_barceloneta.description: The city beach — golden sand, chiringuitos and a boardwalk made for sunset strolls and seafood paella.

s_gothic.name: Gothic Quarter
s_gothic.description: Get lost in narrow medieval lanes, hidden plazas and the Roman walls at the heart of old Barcelona.

s_hagia.name: Hagia Sophia
s_hagia.description: Fifteen centuries of history under one colossal dome — Byzantine cathedral, Ottoman mosque, and breathtaking mosaics.

s_blue_mosque.name: Blue Mosque
s_blue_mosque.description: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, ringed by six minarets and lined with 20,000 hand-painted İznik tiles. Free to enter outside prayer.

s_grand_bazaar.name: Grand Bazaar
s_grand_bazaar.description: One of the world's oldest covered markets — 4,000 shops of lanterns, carpets, spices and gold. Haggling expected.

s_galata.name: Galata Tower
s_galata.description: A medieval stone tower with a panoramic balcony over the Golden Horn, the Bosphorus and the old city rooftops.

s_ortakoy.name: Ortaköy Waterfront
s_ortakoy.description: A buzzy Bosphorus square under the bridge — grab a stuffed kumpir potato and watch the ferries glide by.

s_rijks.name: Rijksmuseum
s_rijks.description: The Dutch Golden Age in one grand building — Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer's quiet masterpieces.

s_vondel.name: Vondelpark
s_vondel.description: Amsterdam's green living room — cycle the loops, picnic on the lawns and catch free summer concerts.

s_jordaan.name: Jordaan Canals
s_jordaan.description: The prettiest quarter — gabled houses, flower-lined bridges and cosy brown cafés down every lane.

s_sensoji.name: Sensō-ji Temple
s_sensoji.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, reached through the giant Kaminarimon lantern and a street of traditional snack stalls.

s_shibuya.name: Shibuya Crossing
s_shibuya.description: The world's busiest pedestrian scramble. Watch the wave from the Starbucks window, then dive into the neon.

s_tsukiji.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
s_tsukiji.description: Go early and graze: the freshest sushi, tamagoyaki on a stick and grilled scallops from market stalls.

s_teamlab.name: teamLab Planets
s_teamlab.description: Wade barefoot through water and infinite mirrored light in this immersive digital-art museum. Book ahead.

s_central_park.name: Central Park
s_central_park.description: 843 acres of lawns, lakes and skyline. Rent a rowboat at the Loeb Boathouse or just wander Bethesda Terrace.

s_top_rock.name: Top of the Rock
s_top_rock.description: The best skyline view in the city — because this is the one that actually includes the Empire State Building.

s_met.name: The Met
s_met.description: Two million works from Egyptian temples to Rooftop sculpture — one of the great museums of the world.

s_brooklyn_bridge.name: Brooklyn Bridge
s_brooklyn_bridge.description: Walk the wooden promenade from Manhattan to DUMBO at dawn for the gothic arches and a clean shot of the skyline.

s_burj.name: Burj Khalifa — At the Top
s_burj.description: The world's tallest building. Ride to the 124th-floor deck for sunset, then watch the fountain show below.

s_dubai_mall.name: The Dubai Mall
s_dubai_mall.description: Beyond shopping: an aquarium, an indoor waterfall and the dancing Dubai Fountain right outside.

s_jumeirah.name: Jumeirah Public Beach
s_jumeirah.description: Soft white sand with a postcard view of the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab — free, with showers and cafés nearby.

s_belem.name: Belém Tower
s_belem.description: A jewel-box fortress on the Tagus from the Age of Discovery — pair it with a warm pastel de nata nearby.

s_alfama.name: Alfama & Miradouro
s_alfama.description: Tangled medieval lanes climbing to terrace viewpoints where fado drifts out of tiny taverns at night.

s_timeout.name: Time Out Market
s_timeout.description: The city's best chefs under one roof — order from a dozen stalls and share at the long communal tables.

s_pending_sequoia.name: Sequoia Nile Lounge
s_pending_sequoia.description: A breezy riverside lounge on the tip of Zamalek with shisha and a view of the water. Submitted for review.

s_pending_teufelsberg.name: Teufelsberg
s_pending_teufelsberg.description: An abandoned Cold-War listening station on an artificial hill, now covered in street art. Submitted for review.

s_pending_sky_bar.name: Leblon Rooftop Bar
s_pending_sky_bar.description: A new speakeasy-style rooftop with skyline cocktails near the Gherkin. Submitted for review.

s_pending_ramen.name: Ichiban Ramen Bar
s_pending_ramen.description: A tiny 8-seat counter doing rich tonkotsu ramen in Shinjuku's back alleys. Submitted for review.

s_marienplatz.name: Marienplatz & Glockenspiel
s_marienplatz.description: Munich's grand central square, framed by the neo-Gothic New Town Hall. Time your visit for the Glockenspiel show at 11am, then wander to the Viktualienmarkt for lunch.

s_englischer_garten.name: Englischer Garten
s_englischer_garten.description: One of the world's largest urban parks — watch the river surfers at the Eisbach wave, then follow the streams to a beer garden under the chestnut trees.

s_roemerberg.name: Römerberg Old Town
s_roemerberg.description: Frankfurt's postcard square of half-timbered houses, rebuilt to its medieval glory. Best at golden hour, with the skyline towers rising behind the gables.

r1.comment: Got there for opening and had the desert almost to myself. Unreal. Negotiate your camel ride price up front!

r2.comment: Bigger than you can imagine. Bring water and a hat — there is zero shade.

r3.comment: Best 40 EGP I spent in Egypt. The garlic-vinegar sauce makes it.

r4.comment: Sunset here is magic. Go early on weekends or you will queue for the lift.

r5.comment: Wandered without a plan and ate the best cacio e pepe of my life. Pure Rome.

r6.comment: Came at 6am for photos with nobody around — completely worth the early alarm.

r7.comment: Skip the funicular and walk up through the back lanes. Quieter and prettier.

r8.comment: Touristy now but still atmospheric. Order the mint tea and just soak it in.

r9.comment: No photo prepares you for the light inside at mid-morning. Book the towers too.

r10.comment: Stunning, but go with a timed ticket or you will wait an hour.

r11.comment: Standing under that dome is humbling. Came at opening and nearly had it to myself.

r12.comment: Rented a rowboat on the lake at golden hour — pure magic with the skyline behind.

r13.comment: The glass floor walkway is a fun touch. Time it for a bridge lift if you can.

r14.comment: Free, vast, and the Egyptian rooms are unreal. Give it a full morning.

r15.comment: Free rooftop with a cocktail in hand — book ahead, slots vanish fast.

r16.comment: Go before 8am for empty photos, then snack your way down Nakamise street.

r17.comment: Roll up your trousers — you walk through water and light. Unlike anything else.

r18.comment: Best tamago and scallops of my life, all before 9am. Bring cash.

r19.comment: Sunset slot is worth the premium. The fountain show afterwards is the bonus.

r20.comment: Beautiful but busy — first entry slot is the move. The view over the city is huge.

r21.comment: Came at 6:30am and had the fountain almost alone. By 10am it is a wall of people.

r22.comment: Grazed my way through cheese, a salt-beef bagel and a brownie. No regrets.

r23.comment: Free, and the spiral up the glass dome at dusk is gorgeous. Just register ahead.

r24.comment: Got lost on purpose and stumbled into fado drifting from a tiny tavern. Lisbon at its best.

r25.comment: Walk it at sunrise from the Brooklyn side — empty, golden, and that skyline.

r26.comment: Overwhelming in the best way. Book the first slot or you are shuffling in a crowd.

r27.comment: Loaded kumpir potato by the water under the bridge — cheap, huge, delicious.

r28.comment: Sailing the Nile as the lights came on was the highlight of Cairo for me.
